section: Land reforms - abolition of intermediaries, tenancy reform, ceiling laws, consolidation; outcomes
subsections: Components of land reforms - what is and is not included; first State
Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments

accepted.s: Which one of the following is included among the components of land reforms in India?
accepted.x: Abolition of intermediaries is a recognised component of land reforms, along with tenancy reform, ceiling, consolidation, cooperative farming and computerisation of land records.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise reform measure while rejecting reversed or extreme formulations.
accepted.sec: Components of land reforms - what is and is not included; first State  [other exams]

accepted.s: Raj Krishna classified land reforms into which one of the following categories?
accepted.x: Raj Krishna grouped land reforms as liberative, distributive, organisational and developmental.
accepted.tq: Direct recall of a named classification.
accepted.sec: Components of land reforms - what is and is not included; first State  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following reforms is correctly matched with Raj Krishna’s category?
accepted.x: Abolition of intermediaries is a liberative reform. Distributive reforms include redistribution, consolidation and tenancy reform.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair and eliminate category reversals.
accepted.sec: Components of land reforms - what is and is not included; first State  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding land reforms:
1. Cooperative farming is included among the components of land reforms.
2. Computerisation of land records is included among the components of land reforms.
3. Industrial licensing is included among the components of land reforms.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Cooperative farming and computerisation of land records are components of land reforms. Industrial licensing is an industrial-policy measure, not a land-reform component.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated policy area inserted among genuine land-reform measures.
accepted.sec: Components of land reforms - what is and is not included; first State  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which category of land reform primarily refers to the abolition of intermediaries?
accepted.x: The abolition of intermediaries is classified by Raj Krishna as a liberative land reform.
accepted.tq: Match the reform action with its exact conceptual category.
accepted.sec: Components of land reforms - what is and is not included; first State  [other exams]

accepted.s: Abolition of intermediaries is generally regarded as the most successful land reform because it brought approximately how many tenants into direct contact with the State?
accepted.x: Abolition of intermediaries brought about 2 crore tenants into direct contact with the State.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the crore-scale figure from nearby lakh and crore distractors.
accepted.sec: Components of land reforms - what is and is not included; first State  [other exams]

accepted.s: The abolition of intermediaries covered approximately what proportion of the cultivated area?
accepted.x: The abolition of intermediaries covered approximately 40 percent of the cultivated area and is considered the most successful land reform.
accepted.tq: Use the exact percentage rather than a broad qualitative estimate.
accepted.sec: Components of land reforms - what is and is not included; first State  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which State is identified as the first State to abolish zamindari in 1950?
accepted.x: Uttar Pradesh is identified in the cited account as the first State to abolish zamindari in 1950. Madras enacted an earlier law in 1948, creating a commonly noted distinction.
accepted.tq: Separate the stated first State from the earlier Madras enactment.
accepted.sec: Components of land reforms - what is and is not included; first State  [other exams]

accepted.s: The two broad phases of land reforms in India are correctly represented by which one of the following?
o: Phase I: 1947– them; Phase II: 1980 onwards
accepted.x: The first phase extended from 1947 to 1970, while the second phase began in 1970 and continued thereafter.
accepted.tq: Fix the boundary year before comparing the two phases.
accepted.sec: Components of land reforms - what is and is not included; first State  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which Constitutional Amendment inserted Articles 31A and 31B and added the Ninth Schedule?
accepted.x: The First Amendment Act of 1951 inserted Articles 31A and 31B and created the Ninth Schedule in the context of land-reform protection.
accepted.tq: Link the constitutional provisions to the amendment that introduced them.
accepted.sec: Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s: The insertion of Articles 31A, 31B and the Ninth Schedule was associated with which case?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu
accepted.x: The insertion of Articles 31A and 31B and the Ninth Schedule followed the constitutional issues highlighted in Kameshwar Singh v. Bihar.
accepted.tq: Apply the wrong-case trap by distinguishing the cases associated with different constitutional stages.
accepted.sec: Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of the Fourth Amendment Act, 1955 in relation to land reforms?
o: It restated Article 31(2) and widened Article 31A to cover zamindari abolition, planning and mineral control.
It subjected all Ninth Schedule laws to Basic Structure review.
It inserted Articles 31A and 31B for the first time.
It inserted Article 31C and abolished the Ninth Schedule.
accepted.x: The Fourth Amendment Act of 1955 restated Article 31(2) and widened Article 31A to zamindari abolition, planning and mineral control.
accepted.tq: Match the amendment with its specific constitutional changes.
accepted.sec: Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Seventeenth Amendment Act, 1964:
1. It widened the meaning of ‘estate’.
2. It provided that land under personal cultivation within the ceiling could be acquired only at market value.
3. It inserted Article 31C.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Seventeenth Amendment widened ‘estate’ and addressed acquisition of land under personal cultivation within the ceiling at market value. Article 31C was inserted by the Twenty-fifth Amendment, not the Seventeenth.
accepted.tq: Use the amendment-number trap to separate closely related constitutional changes.
accepted.sec: Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s: Article 31C was inserted by which Constitutional Amendment?
accepted.x: The Twenty-fifth Amendment Act of 1971 inserted Article 31C.
accepted.tq: Directly link the Article number with its amendment year.
accepted.sec: Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. First Amendment — Articles 31A, 31B and Ninth Schedule
2. Fourth Amendment — Widening of Article 31A
3. Twenty-fifth Amendment — Article 31C
4. Seventeenth Amendment — Widening of ‘estate’
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All four pairs are correct: the First, Fourth, Seventeenth and Twenty-fifth Amendments made the respective changes listed.
accepted.tq: Verify each amendment independently before selecting the inclusive code.
accepted.sec: Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Thirty-fourth and Sixty-sixth Constitutional Amendments together related to which one of the following?
o: Insertion of Article 31C for the first time
Abolition of the ceiling on landholdings
Placement of additional land laws in the Ninth Schedule
accepted.x: The Thirty-fourth Amendment of 1974 and the Sixty-sixth Amendment of 1990 placed additional land laws in the Ninth Schedule, including 55 State Acts, among them Acts of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Identify the common constitutional outcome of two amendment numbers.
accepted.sec: Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s: How many more land laws were placed in the Ninth Schedule through the Thirty-fourth and Sixty-sixth Amendments, as stated in the constitutional land-reform account?
accepted.x: The stated figure is 20 more land laws. The same account also refers to 55 State Acts, including Acts of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Separate the figure for additional laws from the separate count of State Acts.
accepted.sec: Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s:
With reference to I.R. Coelho judgment, consider the following statements:
1. Laws added to the Ninth Schedule after 24 April 1973 can be subjected to Basic Structure review.
2. The relevant cut-off date is associated with the Kesavananda Bharati judgment.
3. Every Ninth Schedule law is permanently beyond judicial review.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: I.R. Coelho held that Ninth Schedule laws added after 24 April 1973 are open to Basic Structure review. The date is linked to Kesavananda Bharati; Ninth Schedule placement does not make every law permanently immune from review.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute immunity statement and retain the date-based rule.
accepted.sec: Constitutional support - Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A-31C, amendments  [other exams]

accepted.s: Consolidation of holdings achieved comparatively greater success in which group of regions?
o: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: Consolidation succeeded in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, while it made little progress in southern and eastern States.
accepted.tq: Match the regional outcome with the correct geographical cluster.
accepted.sec: Consolidation of holdings and Bhoodan-Gramdan

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the regional pattern of progress in consolidation of holdings?
o: It succeeded in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, with little progress in southern and eastern States.
It progressed substantially in southern and eastern States but not in northern India.
It was confined exclusively to Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
accepted.x: The major success occurred in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, whereas southern and eastern States saw little progress.
accepted.tq: Test the reversed regional comparison commonly used as a distractor.
accepted.sec: Consolidation of holdings and Bhoodan-Gramdan

accepted.s: Acharya Vinoba Bhave launched the Bhoodan movement at which place?
accepted.x: Bhoodan was initiated by Acharya Vinoba Bhave at Pochampally in Nalgonda, Telangana, in 1951.
accepted.tq: Use the precise place-name and district-location combination.
accepted.sec: Consolidation of holdings and Bhoodan-Gramdan

accepted.s: Bhoodan movement was initiated on which date?
accepted.x: The Bhoodan movement began at Pochampally on 18 April 1951.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the exact day and month from nearby national dates.
accepted.sec: Consolidation of holdings and Bhoodan-Gramdan

accepted.s: What proportion of land did Acharya Vinoba Bhave appeal to landowners to donate under the Bhoodan movement?
accepted.x: The appeal under Bhoodan was for the donation of one-sixth of the land.
accepted.tq: Recall the fractional figure precisely rather than relying on a general impression of donation.
accepted.sec: Consolidation of holdings and Bhoodan-Gramdan

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Bhoodan movement:
1. It was initiated by Acharya Vinoba Bhave.
2. It began at Pochampally amid the Telangana armed struggle.
3. More than 40 lakh acres were pledged, although much of the land was barren.
4. It later led to the Gramdan movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Bhoodan began at Pochampally in 1951, involved pledges exceeding 40 lakh acres, much of it barren, and subsequently led to Gramdan.
accepted.tq: Check the sequence of founder, context, quantitative outcome and later development.
accepted.sec: Consolidation of holdings and Bhoodan-Gramdan

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. First Amendment inserting Articles 31A and 31B
B. Seventeenth Amendment widening the meaning of ‘estate’
C. Twenty-fifth Amendment inserting Article 31C
D. I.R. Coelho judgment
Select the correct answer using the code given below.

accepted.s: The 75th anniversary of the First Amendment is scheduled to fall on which date in 2026?
accepted.x: The 75th anniversary of the First Amendment is marked on 18 June 2026 in the stated current-affairs reference.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the anniversary date from other important constitutional and land-reform dates.

accepted.s: The Andhra Pradesh proposal to decriminalise offences under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling) Act, 1973 concerns how many offences out of the total mentioned?
accepted.x: The proposal concerns decriminalising two offences among the 42 offences under the AP Land Reforms (Ceiling) Act, 1973.
accepted.tq: Keep the smaller targeted count separate from the total number of offences.

accepted.s: Which one of the following best reflects the criticism concerning the present distribution of landholdings?
o: About 28.9 percent of land is held by farmers with 0–1 hectare holdings.
About 28.9 percent of land is held exclusively by farmers with more than 10 hectares.
Exactly 50 percent of land is held by marginal farmers.
Land distribution has become completely even after ceiling legislation.
accepted.x: The stated criticism is that about 28.9 percent of land is with farmers holding 0–1 hectare. Leasing reform and digitisation of land records have been urged in response to continuing skewness.
accepted.tq: Use the exact percentage and holding-size range while rejecting reversed or absolute claims.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: Which two measures have been urged in debates concerning continuing skewness in land distribution?
o: Expansion of zamindari and suspension of consolidation
Abolition of tenancy and removal of land records
accepted.x: Leasing reform and digitisation of land records have been urged to address continuing problems in land distribution and land administration.
accepted.tq: Identify the policy response that directly addresses the stated land-governance problems.
accepted.sec: Universal angles

accepted.s: The Srikakulam Naxalite unrest and the droughts of 1966–69 contributed to which development in Andhra Pradesh?
o: They led to the creation of the Ninth Schedule in 1951.
They ended the first phase of land reforms in India in 1950.
They resulted in the abolition of consolidation of holdings.
They pushed the second phase of land reforms in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.x: The Srikakulam Naxalite unrest and the droughts of 1966–69 pushed Phase II of land reforms in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Connect the regional disturbances and drought period with the policy phase they influenced.
accepted.sec: Universal angles
